choices.description:
Choices for the question, empty the first time. To change an assumption or answer a clarification, send the
same question with `choices` of the previous answer, the changed entry replaced or added. A question whose text
was edited is a new question: send `choices` empty. The backend does not compare with earlier questions; it
applies the choices it recognizes for this question and ignores the others with a warning
`choice_not_applied`. Choices not listed use their default.

AskResponse.description: Answer to one question, with the evidence behind it. See `AskStatus` for which fields are set.

choices.description:
Every choice this answer used, defaults included, in the shape of `AskRequest.choices`. To ask again with one
choice changed, send this list with that entry replaced; for `needs_choice`, send it plus a pick for each
clarification. Choices the backend did not recognize are not in it.

clarifications.description: Questions back to the user, only for `needs_choice`. Every entry has `selected` null.

message.description:
Text for the end user (Vietnamese): the reason for `rejected` and `failed`, the prompt for `needs_choice`;
null for `answered`.

model.description: Language model configured for the question, for example `gemini-2.5-flash` or `mock`.

query_id.description: Id of the question in the history (`queries`); null for `needs_choice`.

sql_generated.description: SQL written by the model, on logical table names. After a fix round, the fixed SQL.

sql_guarded.description:
SQL that ran: the generated SQL after the guard added row-level filters and a row limit. Still on logical table
names, no file paths.

steps.description:
What the backend did, in order, with timings. A step may appear twice, for example `run` before and after a
`repair`.

version_id.description: Dataset version the question ran on.

warnings.description: Notes shown next to the result; they never hide it.

AskStatus.description:
Outcome of the question, and which fields of `AskResponse` are set:
- `answered`: the SQL ran. Set: `query_id`, `sql_generated`, `sql_guarded`, `understanding`, `result`; `chart`
  when a chart fits; `explanation` for a "why" question (when the breakdown cannot be made, a warning
  `explanation_unavailable` says why).
- `needs_choice`: the question can be read several ways; pick one option of each entry in `clarifications` and ask
  again. This can happen before the model is called (a word matches several columns) or after (the two slices of
  a "why" question cannot be told). Set: `message`, `clarifications`; `sql_generated` when the model was called.
  Not recorded in the history, so `query_id` is null.
- `rejected`: the guard refused the SQL: the generated one for a reason a fix cannot change (for example it is not
  a read-only SELECT, or it calls a function that is not allowed), or the one fixed in the `repair` round. Set:
  `message` (the reason), `query_id`, `sql_generated`; the `guard` step that stopped it has `ok` false.
- `failed`: the SQL could not run and the one fix round did not help, either because the fixed SQL failed too or
  because the model failed during the fix; or the SQL ran past the time or memory limit, which gets no fix round.
  Set: `message`, `query_id`, `sql_generated`; `sql_guarded` unless that SQL never passed the guard. The `run` or
  `repair` step that stopped it has `ok` false.

A fix round starts when the analytics engine fails on the SQL, or when the guard refuses it because a table or
column does not exist or because it could build a value too large (too deep, too many concatenated pieces, too
wide, a size argument over the limit); there is at most one round per question. The status names the step that stopped the
question: the guard gives `rejected`, the engine or the fix round gives `failed`. A model error before any SQL
exists is not a status: the request gets 502 or 503.

detail.description: Text for the end user (Vietnamese), for example the guard's reason or the engine error.

ok.description:
False for a step that failed. A failed step does not always stop the question: a failed `run` or `guard` can be
followed by `repair`, a failed `narrate` by a template summary. `AskStatus` tells whether the question stopped.

email.description: Email of an active account; it becomes `admin` of the workspace.

CellValue.description: One cell: a JSON number, string or boolean; read it with the `kind` of its column.

ChartKind.description: `bar` for one dimension and one measure, `line` when the x axis is time.

ChartSuggestion.description: Suggested chart; null in `AskResponse` when the result is better shown as a table only.

x.description: Column on the x axis: a dimension for `bar`, time for `line`. A name from `result.columns`.

y.description: Columns drawn as series, names from `result.columns`.

Choice.description:
A point where the question can be read several ways. To change it, ask the same question again with
`AskResponse.choices`, the entry for this `id` replaced.

label.description: Text for the end user (Vietnamese): what can be read several ways, for example which column a word means.

selected.description: Id of the option in use; null when the user has to pick (`needs_choice`).

id.description: Opaque id set by the backend; send it back unchanged.

ChosenOption.description:
The pick for one `Choice`. A `choice_id` or `option_id` the backend does not recognize (for example a choice that
no longer applies) is ignored, left out of `AskResponse.choices`, and reported with a warning `choice_not_applied`:
an assumption falls back to its default, a clarification is asked again.

option_id.description: One of the `ChoiceOption.id` of that choice.

ColumnRole.description:
What a result column is:
- `dimension`: a grouping key that is not time, for example a market.
- `time`: a grouping key on time, for example a quarter.
- `measure`: an aggregate, for example a sum; its cells can be drilled into.
- `other`: anything else, for example a column of a query without aggregates.

name.description: 1 to 100 characters. The slug is derived from it.

logical_table.description: Table name used in SQL, derived from the dataset name.

DimensionBreakdown.description: Contribution of every group of one dimension; the contributions add up to `change`.

column.description: Dimension column, as named in the dataset (not a name from `result.columns`).

groups.description: Every group of the column, largest contribution (by absolute value) first.

kind.description: How to read the group values, like the `kind` of a result column.

sql.description: SQL that computed the groups of both slices, after the guard.

ErrorBody.description: Error body returned by every endpoint on failure.

message.description: Human-readable explanation in Vietnamese, meant to be shown to the end user as is.

ErrorCode.description: Stable machine-readable error code; one per HTTP status.

Explanation.description:
Breakdown of a change between two slices (two periods or two groups); null in `AskResponse` unless an answered
"why" question has one. Numbers are exact strings of decimal digits.

dimensions.description: One breakdown per dimension, the dimension that explains the change best first.

measure.description: Measure that changed, text for the end user (Vietnamese).

summary.description: Plain-language summary for the end user (Vietnamese). Every number in it appears in this breakdown.

summary_by_model.description:
False when the model's text failed the number check, or the model was not reached, and `summary` is a template
sentence written by the backend.

filter.description: SQL condition that selects the rows of the slice, on logical names.

label.description: Text for the end user (Vietnamese) naming the slice, for example a quarter.

value.description: Value of the measure on the slice.

GroupContribution.description: One group of a dimension. `value` is null for the group of rows where the dimension column is null.

oneOf.description: Value of the dimension column for this group; null for rows where it is null.

ListSheetsRequest.description: Multipart form for listing the sheets of an Excel file. The file is not stored.

workspaces.description: Workspaces the user belongs to, with their role in each, sorted by name.

Membership.description: A workspace the user belongs to, with their role in it.

temporary_password.description: Shown once to hand to the user; not stored anywhere in plain text.

name.description:
Column name as the SQL returns it, made unique: from left to right, a name already used gets the smallest
suffix `_2`, `_3`, ... that no column has, so `a, a, a_2` becomes `a, a_3, a_2`.

ResultTable.description: Rows of the result; null in `AskResponse` unless the status is `answered`. At most 1000 rows are sent.

limit_reached.description:
True when `total_rows` equals the guard's row cap (whether the guard added the LIMIT or lowered one the SQL
had): the full result may have more rows, so show
`total_rows` as "at least".

rows.description: One array per row, cells in the order of `columns`; null is a SQL NULL.

total_rows.description: Number of rows `sql_guarded` returned. This is the full result unless `limit_reached`.

truncated.description: True when `rows` holds fewer rows than `total_rows`.

setup_code.description: Code printed in the backend log at startup; case and surrounding spaces are ignored.

workspace_name.description: Name of the first workspace; empty gives a default name.

needed.description: True while the installation has no account yet: show the first-run setup screen instead of sign-in.

SheetSummary.description: A sheet of an Excel file, as shown when choosing sheets to upload.

approx_rows.description:
Rows below the header, from the data range the file records. An estimate: may include empty rows, 0 when the
file does not record it.

columns.description: Column names from the header row, normalised as on upload; empty if the sheet has no data.

hidden.description: Hidden in Excel. Hidden sheets are skipped when no sheet is chosen.

StepName.description:
Step of the backend:
- `context`: read the dataset profile and build the prompt.
- `llm`: the language model writes SQL.
- `guard`: check the SQL, add row-level filters and a row limit.
- `run`: run the SQL on the analytics engine.
- `repair`: the language model fixes SQL that failed to run, or that the guard refused because a table or column
  does not exist or because it could build a value too large (at most once).
- `explain`: compute the breakdown of a "why" question (code, no model).
- `narrate`: the language model writes the summary of the breakdown.
- `record`: save the question in the history.

Understanding.description:
The "understood as" card, built from `sql_guarded`: what is measured, filtered, grouped, sorted, over which
period, and the assumptions made. Null in `AskResponse` unless the status is `answered`. `limit` is null when only
the guard's row cap applies; `time_range` is null when the SQL has no time filter.

assumptions.description: Assumptions the user can change, including clarifications answered earlier; every entry has `selected` set.

filters.description:
Filters of the question, then the row-level filters the guard added for the user's data role (the label says
which).

oneOf.description: Row limit the question asked for, for example the top 3; null when only the guard's limit applies.
Period the question covers; null when the SQL has no time filter.

UnderstoodItem.description: One thing the question was understood to mean.

label.description: Text for the end user (Vietnamese) naming the measure, filter, grouping, order or period.

sql.description: Fragment of `sql_guarded` this item comes from.

UploadDatasetRequest.description: Multipart form for uploading a dataset. Total size is limited by MAX_UPLOAD_MB (413 above it).

dataset_id.description: Add a new version to this dataset instead of creating a new one.

file.description:
One or more CSV or Parquet files (repeat the field), or one Excel `.xlsx` file. Files with the same columns are
stacked into one table.

name.description: Name of the new dataset; defaults to the first file name.

sheet.description:
Sheet of the Excel file to upload; repeat to stack several sheets with the same columns. Not needed when the
file has one sheet.

columns.description: Columns of the new table; empty when `created` is false.

created.description: False when the files match an existing version: nothing new was created.

UserSummary.description: An account in the system administrator's list.

ValueKind.description:
How to read the cells of a column, decided by the column type. Any cell may also be null (SQL NULL).
- `text`: JSON string.
- `number`: JSON number, for types a JavaScript number holds exactly: integers up to 32 bits, FLOAT, DOUBLE. NaN
  and infinity are sent as null.
- `decimal`: JSON string of decimal digits, integer or not, for example "5000" or "-1234.50", for BIGINT
  (COUNT returns one), HUGEINT, unsigned 64 and 128 bit integers and DECIMAL, which a JavaScript number would
  round. Convert with `Number()` only to draw a chart or to sort; comparing the strings sorts "10" before "9".
- `boolean`: JSON boolean.
- `date`: JSON string `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- `timestamp`: JSON string in ISO 8601, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.ffffff]` for TIMESTAMP (no time zone, as stored),
  ending in `Z` for TIMESTAMPTZ (converted to UTC).
- `other`: JSON string as the analytics engine prints the value: TIME, INTERVAL, lists, structs and other types.

A `date` or `timestamp` with a year after 9999 or before 1 AD uses the ISO 8601 expanded form: `+10000-01-01`;
year 1 BC is `0000`, 2 BC is `-0001`. Infinite dates and times are sent as null. A result column of type TIME_NS,
TIME WITH TIME ZONE, BIT, BIGNUM, VARIANT, GEOMETRY or a type the backend does not recognize is not read: the `run`
step fails and the fix round casts it to text.

llm.description: Language model provider in use, for example `mock` or `gemini-2.5-flash`.

VolumePrice.description:
Change split into a volume effect and a price effect, for a measure that is volume times price (for example
orders times average order value); null in `Explanation` for other measures.

base_price.description: Measure divided by volume, rounded to a fixed number of decimals; the only rounded numbers here.

if_volume_unchanged.description: Value of the measure if the volume had stayed at `base_volume`: `base_volume * compare_price`.

price_effect.description: `change - volume_effect`, so that the two effects add up to `change` exactly.

price_label.description: Text for the end user (Vietnamese) naming the price, for example the average order value.

sql.description: SQL that computed the volume and the measure of both slices, after the guard.

volume_effect.description: `(compare_volume - base_volume) * (base_price + compare_price) / 2`, exact from the rounded prices.

volume_label.description: Text for the end user (Vietnamese) naming the volume, for example the number of orders.

WarningCode.description:
Kind of note:
- `empty_result`: no rows.
- `all_null`: a result column holds only nulls.
- `filter_value_not_found`: the SQL filters on a value that does not occur in the column.
- `unusual_magnitude`: a value is far outside what the data makes likely, for example a ratio above 100%.
- `explanation_unavailable`: a "why" question was answered without a breakdown; the message says why.
- `choice_not_applied`: a choice sent with the question was not recognized and the default was used.

WorkspaceOverview.description: A workspace as the system administrator sees it: name and members, none of its data.
